title: UN Chief: Political Dialogue Solution to Ukraine Crisis
main_content:
United Nations Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon has called for political dialogue between Russia and Ukraine as the solution to the crisis in Ukraine.

Ban made his remarks during a stop in New Zealand Tuesday, a day after Ukrainian separatist leader Andrei Purgin said he is ready to discuss a cease-fire and prisoner exchange.

Purgin spoke at the first round of peace talks that opened Monday in the Belarusian capital, Minsk.

Pro-Russian separatists have said they are willing to remain part of Ukraine if they are granted more autonomy.

Ban is in New Zealand for meetings with Prime Minister John Key.

Also Monday, Ukrainian President Petro Poroshenko accused Russia of “open aggression” in his country.

NATO estimates at least 1,000 Russian troops are in Ukraine. Russia has repeatedly denied it has any troops there.

A Ukrainian spokesman said the army has ordered Ukrainian troops to retreat from the airport near the rebel-held city of Luhansk after an unsuccessful fight against a Russian tank unit. He said seven Ukrainian troops have been killed and 25 wounded since Sunday.

European leaders are accusing Russia of waging war against Ukraine.

questions.question: In what context did Ban Ki-moon call for a political dialogue?
options: During a conference about economic sanctions against Russia
While visiting New Zealand, amidst the ongoing crisis in Ukraine
At a summit focused on NATO's involvement in Eastern Europe
In response to a cease-fire proposed by Ukrainian President Petro Poroshenko
questions.answer: While visiting New Zealand, amidst the ongoing crisis in Ukraine
